meta.title: Mohammed Al-Shaikh | Estates, Waqf & Wills Lawyer

hero.title: Preserving legacy,
hero.subtitle: Precise counsel for estate administration and division, waqf structuring and governance, and wills—protecting rights while reducing the risk of dispute.

about.title: Legal knowledge grounded in Sharia and practical experience
about.statement: Estates and endowments concern more than assets; they protect family rights, preserve lasting impact, and honor the intentions of the deceased, donor, and testator.
about.paragraphOne: Mohammed bin Abdulwahid bin Ahmed Al-Shaikh is a licensed attorney and notary. He earned his Bachelor of Laws from King Faisal University with distinction and first-class honors, and completed the Ministry of Justice Judicial Training Center's lawyer qualification program.
about.paragraphTwo: His practical experience in personal status courts focuses on estate division and related disputes, alongside waqf structuring, governance, and wills. A co-founder of Ufuq Al-Hikma Law Firm, he combines Sharia grounding with rigorous legal practice.

services.title: Focused work for family wealth and enduring legacy

items.title: Estates & Division
items.description: A full review of estate assets, liabilities, and rights, through consensual or judicial division and the resolution of disputes among heirs.

items.title: Waqf & Governance
items.description: Establishing and organizing endowments, drafting deeds and governance rules, and protecting the donor's conditions and the endowment's continuity.

items.title: Wills
items.description: Drafting, reviewing, and notarizing wills, with counsel on validity, implementation, and legal or Sharia limitations.

process.title: From complexity to a clear path
process.description: Each matter begins with the facts, documents, and relationships between the parties, followed by a path that joins Sharia principles, legal procedure, and practical resolution.

items.title: Understand
items.description: An initial review of the parties, rights, documents, and genuine points of dispute.

items.title: Analyze
items.description: Legal and Sharia assessment of the file, options, and risks before action.

items.title: Plan
items.description: Selecting a consensual or judicial route with defined stages and responsibilities.

items.title: Execute
items.description: Careful representation and follow-through until the required division, structure, or notarization is completed.

credentials.title: Training across law and jurisprudence
credentials.description: A dual foundation for understanding estate, waqf, and will matters through both legal and Sharia perspectives.
